notes:
Summary: Sirocco Relay builds a distributed contact center orchestration layer for midsize telco support teams. They want a multilingual automation stack that keeps regional tone and legal constraints intact. Key asks:

- Workloads: real-time agent assist (live chat + voice RT transcripts), automated ticket summarization (end-of-day rolls), and tool-calling (Zendesk macros, CRM updates). Also periodic batch reranking for knowledge-base search.
- Traffic profile: baseline 40–60 rps for agent assist; burst capacity to 220 rps during incident spikes (outages). Need graceful degradation under spikes — prefer Dedicated + hosted fallbacks.
- Latency/throughput targets: tail latency <= 350ms for agent assist (95th), token cost sensitivity for summarization and reranking.
- Multilingual needs: support for en-US (friendly/concise), de-DE (formal, use Sie), fr-CA (neutral, cultural variants), es-MX (informal). Must preserve locale-aware tone profiles and per-language glossaries.
- Routing/fallback policy: route to region-preferred models where available; failover to quantized smaller model for non-critical summarize jobs. Want per-language cache warming (prefix caching) to reduce cold-start for scripted dialogs.
- Security/compliance: SOC2 required, SSO/SAML integration, audit logging for all tool-calls, optional KMS for key management, strict EU data residency for EU customers.
- Integrations: Zendesk (macros & ticket fields), Twilio (webhook + voice transcript), internal CRM (tool-calls to update case_state). POC includes small Zendesk sandbox.
- POC success metrics: 1) maintain agent assist 95th latency <=350ms under 2x baseline load; 2) summarization accuracy F1 >= 0.78 on annotated set; 3) zero missed tool-calls in 500-run playbook; 4) audit log completeness for 30 days.

Direct quotes / paraphrases from stakeholders:
- "Tone matters — we can't have German responses use tu when formal Sie is expected." — Head of Localization
- "If a spike hits, we need predictable fallbacks — can't have escalations failing silently." — Director of Support Ops
